# PhysicsFinger

**Class** · namespace `VRFramework.Interaction.Runtime` · assembly `VRFramework.Interaction.Runtime` · [view source](https://git.cie-group.cz/vr-framework/vrf4/core/-/blob/interaction/physics-hold/Runtime/Scripts/Interaction/PhysicsFinger.cs#L18)

One finger's own body: a small rigidbody chasing the tip of a tracked finger, which the world can
stop and which can push things about.

The finger equivalent of [`PhysicsHand`](/api/vrframework-interaction-runtime/PhysicsHand), and driven the same way: a clamped
velocity controller with a force ceiling. The ceiling is the finger's strength - it decides
what a poke can shove aside and how hard a fingertip presses into a surface before it gives
up and lags behind.

Not jointed to the hand. What a blocked finger sends back to the arm is sent as a force
instead, by whatever owns it - see [`PhysicsFingers`](/api/vrframework-interaction-runtime/PhysicsFingers).

```csharp
[ExecuteAlways]
[RequireComponent(typeof(Rigidbody))]
public class PhysicsFinger : MonoBehaviour
```

### Push {#push}

What the finger pushed against last step, in newtons.

The force it was asked for while it was not free to move. A finger pressing on something
is pressing back on the arm just as hard, and this is what that reaction is built from.
